Trinity River National Water Trail
Master Plan Update
Jai-W Hayes-Jackson and Erin Blackman,
NCTCOG

Purpose
In 2018, Trinity Coalition and NCTCOG met with cities and counties with a proposal to
integrate the 21 existing canoe launch sites into a single paddling trail. In October
2020, the Trinity River Paddling Trail was designated as a National Water Trail by the
National Park Service.
The Trinity River National Water Trail Task Force and master plan is a coordinated
effort between:
 The Trinity Coalition,
 The North Central Texas Council of Governments,
 and the communities and organizations along the Trinity River.
The Trinity River National Water Trail Master Plan seeks to identify long range actions
that advance recreation, tourism, and economic development along the Water Trail.
This plan will help guide communities with developing the trail and how to allocate
resources.

Goals for the Trail
1. Develop new entry sites to shorten
distances between sites
2. Promote the use of the trail and educate
all users
3. Make the trail more accessible to all
4. Maintain condition and safety of the
existing and future launch sites
5. Promote stewardship along the Trinity River
6. Connect the trail to the existing land trails
7. Extend the trail further south
8. Promote the economic benefits of the trail
9. Highlight the cultural and historical context
of the trail

Develop new entry sites to shorten distances
between sites
Actions
• Identify priority gaps in public access along
the water trail.
• Complete priority gaps along the trail.
• Identify common priority projects to
leverage maximum joint investments.

Promote the use of the National Water Trail and
educate all users
Actions
• Increase sharing of information to improve communication with
stakeholders (ex. newsletters, blogs, websites, etc.).
• Identify destinations along the trail in each community to highlight.
• Establish regularly scheduled trail focus meeting for additional stakeholder
input (tourism and visitors’ bureaus, recreation groups, health organizations,
etc.).
• Emphasize the rules and regulations of non-motorized and motorized water
recreation vehicles and other trail related activities.

Make the trail more accessible to all
Actions
• Identify ADA accessible launch sites on the trail.
• Ensure trails are designed and constructed to meet accessibility standards,
including gentle slopes, firm surfaces, and minimal obstacles.
• Regularly maintain the trail to ensure it remains accessible.
• Involve individuals with disabilities or advocacy groups in the planning and
design process to gather insights and feedback for improving accessibility.
• Conduct outreach and educational programs to raise awareness about
trail accessibility, inclusivity, and proper etiquette when sharing the trail
with diverse users.

Maintain condition and safety of the existing and
future launch sites
Actions
• Identify and document best management
practices for trail construction and maintenance.
• Identify existing condition of launch sites to
prioritize needs.
• Enhance tools to electronically collect and
report trail conditions on Trinity Coalition’s
website.
• Maintain cohesive signage throughout the trail
and clearly mark hazard areas.

Promote stewardship along the Trinity River
Actions
• Develop and implement volunteer programs to
increase volunteer engagement in water trails.
• Work with local organizations, schools, businesses,
and government bodies to collectively promote
stewardship.
• Distribute information that educate visitors about
the ecosystem, conservation practices, and the
importance of responsible behavior including
guidelines for proper trail use.

Connect the Trinity River National Water Trail to
the existing land trail
Actions
• Create a recreational map that
includes the water trail, land trails, and
bike paths.
• Promote signage that shows the
Veloweb
relation of the water trail to existing
land trails.
• Highlight community points of
interests.
DFW Discovery Trail

Extend the National Water Trail further south
Actions
• Collaborate with Trinity River Corridor
Councils of Governments (Heart of Texas
Council of Governments, Houston-Galveston
Area Council, Brazos Valley Council of
Governments).
• Expand The National Water Trail Task Force to
additional communities.
• Work with other communities to identify entry
sites for the remainder of the Trinity River.

Promote the economic benefits of the trail
Actions
• Complete additional studies on
the economic impact / value of
trails.
• Collaborate with Tourism Bureaus
to promote ecotourism and
recreational activities.
• Highlight local businesses and
services that cater to recreational
activities.

Highlight the cultural and historical context of the trail
Actions
• Work with indigenous
populations to capture
the cultural context of
the trail.
• Collaborate with schools
and universities to
capture the historic
context of the trail.
